+    # One point per measured operating point. The builder renders one prefill
+    # and one decode worker; the label and description give the lane's worker
+    # counts (each worker is two trays), which the schema cannot express.
+    #
+    # Specialized decode (c16-c32): the latency_specialized backend on decode
+    # needs FULL decode CUDA graphs, FP32 SSM state and no expert parallelism.
+    # --max-num-seqs is 64 // (K + 1) = 12 for the K4 draft, with graphs for
+    # every batch size up to 64. Both roles pin the DCP KV interleave to 1 and

     runbook: |
-      The GB300 AgentX disaggregated lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4047](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047), points refined in [#4373](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4373) and [#4516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4516)) runs Dynamo + vLLM with several prefill and decode workers. Prefill and decode workers are both TP8 + DCP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays; prefill workers also use EP8 with MegaMoE, and decode workers use no expert parallelism. KV moves over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e4a5b5537344b103ed10de7764378ef09604ef3d`, Dynamo `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`.
+      The GB300 AgentX disaggregated lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4047](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047), points refined in [#4373](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4373), [#4516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4516) and [#4638](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4638)) runs Dynamo + vLLM with several prefill and decode workers. Every worker is TP8 + DCP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays; prefill workers also use EP8 with MegaMoE, and decode workers use no expert parallelism. KV moves over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store in host DRAM. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5`), Dynamo built from `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`, Mooncake `0.3.13.post1` from the image.
+
+      | Clients | Prefill workers | Decode workers | GPUs | Decode profile | Decode attention | Decode `--max-num-seqs` |
+      |---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
+      | 16 | 1 | 3 | 32 | Specialized | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 12 |
+      | 24, 32 | 1 | 2 | 24 | Specialized | `TOKENSPEED_MLA` | 12 |
+      | 112, 128 | 2 | 4 | 48 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
+      | 128, 152 | 2 | 3 | 40 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
+      | 240 | 3 | 4 | 56 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
+      | 240, 264 | 3 | 3 | 48 | Regular | `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` | 128 |
+
+      Each point renders one prefill worker and one decode worker; start the table's number of workers per role with the same commands, two trays each. Run every worker command on both of its trays with the same `--master-addr` (the first tray's address), `--nnodes 2` and `--node-rank 0` or `1`. Prefill workers always use `--max-num-seqs 32` and target and draft attention on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`.
 
-      | Clients | Prefill workers | Decode workers | GPUs | Decode profile | Decode `--max-num-seqs` |
-      |---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
-      | 16 | 1 | 3 | 32 | [Specialized](#specialized-decode-low-concurrency) | 12 |
-      | 24-32 | 1 | 2 | 24 | [Specialized](#specialized-decode-low-concurrency) | 12 |
-      | 48-64 | 1 | 2 | 24 | Regular | 128 |
-      | 240 | 2 | 3 | 40 | Regular | 128 |
-      | 240 | 3 | 4 | 56 | Regular | 128 |
+      **Specialized decode (16-32 clients).** The decode workers use the `latency_specialized` decode backend from the [GB300 low-latency preset](#preset-gb300_low_latency). Its requirements are listed there: V2 model runner, FULL decode CUDA graphs, BF16 convolution state with FP32 recurrent state, DSpark with at most 7 draft tokens, no pipeline or expert parallelism, and DCP of 1 or TP. Both roles pin `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`: left unset, NIXL P/D raises the DCP KV interleave to the KV block size after the specialized decode has read it, so its spec-verify causal mask uses the stale value. The prefill workers do not set `--additional-config`, because the backend rejects the expert parallelism they use.
 
-      Prefill workers always use `--max-num-seqs 32`. The regular profile is the Workers commands below; the specialized one changes both roles as described under [Specialized decode](#specialized-decode-low-concurrency).
+      **Regular decode (112-264 clients).** The decode workers run the target and the DSpark draft on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`, an FP8 MLA decode backend that plans its split-KV work on the device; it is never selected automatically, and prefill steps use the configured MLA prefill backend. These points cap decode at 128 sequences with ReplaySSM, so TTFT is not traded for ITL by a standing decode queue.
 
-      The preset renders one prefill pool and one decode pool of the specialized profile (the 1P2D c24-c32 row); its decode uses `--max-num-seqs 12`. For the regular points use the Workers commands below. It turns **Spec decoding** off, because the toggle's generic `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark` K8 draft was not qualified and specialized decode allows at most 7 draft tokens, and **Tool calling** off (see the parser note under Workers). This preset's DCP8 pools do not combine with a DEP decode pool, which renders TP1 with `--decode-context-parallel-size 8` that vLLM rejects; the DEP16 decode lane is the [AgentX 3P1D DEP16 preset](#preset-gb300_agentx_pd_dep16).
+      The preset turns **Spec decoding** off, because the toggle's generic `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark` K8 draft was not qualified and specialized decode allows at most 7 draft tokens, and **Tool calling** off: `python3 -m dynamo.vllm` parses the remaining arguments as vLLM engine arguments only, so the vLLM API-server flags `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser` are rejected there. For tool calling and reasoning output, add `--dyn-tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-enable-structural-tag` to both roles. This preset's DCP8 pools do not combine with a DEP decode pool, which renders TP1 with `--decode-context-parallel-size 8` that vLLM rejects; the DEP16 decode lane is the [AgentX 3P1D DEP16 preset](#preset-gb300_agentx_pd_dep16).
 
-      Documented here only: worker counts beyond one pool per role, the Mooncake store connector (the builder's Mooncake option renders a plain `MooncakeStoreConnector` without the qualified NIXL MultiConnector, recompute policy and load options), the Mooncake services, prefill `--kv-events-config`, and the frontend's router mode and session affinity (the builder renders round-robin).
+      The preset selects the distributed (embedded) Mooncake store on the **KV Offload** row, which wraps NIXL and the `MooncakeStoreConnector` in one `MultiConnector` on both roles; the preset sets the lane's connector options on it (recompute on a failed load, offload off). Documented here only: the worker counts, the lane's Mooncake master options and store sizing (the builder's Mooncake option shows its own defaults), and the frontend's router mode and session affinity (the builder renders round-robin).
 
       ### Services
 
@@ -862,96 +967,14 @@ presets:
         --default_kv_lease_ttl=60000 --eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.95 --eviction_ratio=0.10
       ```
 
-      The workers' Mooncake store uses P2P handshake metadata, RDMA over the node's NICs, a 160GB global segment and a 4GB local buffer, with offload disabled.
-
-      ### Environment (every worker)
-
-      ```bash
-      export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=1 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=1 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=1
-      export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1 VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0 VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0
-      export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL
-      export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS
-      export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=0
-      export VLLM_MOONCAKE_LOAD_RECV_THREADS=4 MC_SLICE_SIZE=1048576 MC_MAX_MR_SIZE=4294967296 MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1
-      export UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n UCX_MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE=n UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024 UCX_TCP_AF_PRIO=inet
-      export TOKENSPEED_MLA_FP16_PARTIALS=0
-      export DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120 ETCD_LEASE_TTL=600
-      export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800 VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT=600000
-      ```
-
-      Set `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` on prefill workers and `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0` on decode workers. Prefill workers also set `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT=1024` and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT=1024`. Loading the 2.8T checkpoint across trays and autotuning takes a while, which is why the engine-ready, execute-model and RPC timeouts are raised.
-
-      ### Workers
+      Every worker reads the Mooncake store configuration from the JSON file that `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` points to. The lane registered 160GB per rank:
 
-      Each worker spans two trays. Run the command on both trays with the same `--master-addr` (the first tray's address), `--nnodes 2` and `--node-rank 0` or `1`.
-
-      Prefill:
-
-      ```bash
-      python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
-        --disaggregation-mode prefill --request-plane tcp \
-        --nnodes 2 --node-rank <0|1> --master-addr <first-tray-ip> --device-ids 0,1,2,3 \
-        --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest

+

+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler
+
+
+def _input_batch(req_ids: list[str], structured: bool) -> InputBatch:
+    num_reqs = len(req_ids)
+    buffers = InputBuffers(num_reqs, num_reqs, torch.device("cuda"))
+    batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, buffers, is_padding=False)
+    return replace(batch, req_ids=req_ids, has_structured_output_reqs=structured)
+
+
+def _set_draft_toks(
+    handler: DraftTokensHandler,
+    req_ids: list[str],
+    tokens: list[list[int]],
+    structured: bool,
+) -> None:
+    batch = _input_batch(req_ids=req_ids, structured=structured)
+    handler.set_draft_tokens(batch, torch.tensor(tokens, device="cuda"))
+
+
+def _get_draft_toks(handler: DraftTokensHandler) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
+    drafts = handler.get_draft_tokens()
+    assert drafts is not None
+    return dict(zip(drafts.req_ids, drafts.draft_token_ids, strict=True))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+def test_draft_tokens_follow_request_lifecycle() -> None:
+    handler = DraftTokensHandler(torch.device("cuda"))
+
+    # The worker samples two structured-output requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[11, 12], [21, 22]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+
+    # "b" finishes before this result is handed back to the scheduler
+    handler.discard("b")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {"a": [11, 12]}
+
+    # "a" continues and "b" is re-added with a new draft row
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[13, 14], [23, 24]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+    }
+
+    # A batch without structured-output must not erase drafts from live requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["plain"],
+        tokens=[[31, 32]],
+        structured=False,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+
+    # Requests finish independently, and the handler is empty once all are gone
+    handler.discard("a")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+    handler.discard("b")
+    handler.discard("plain")

     np.testing.assert_array_equal(
         descs[:, 0], [base[0], base[0] + 256, base[0], base[0] + 256]
     )

+# Real model KV layouts, end to end on CPU: vLLM's planner and allocator build
+# P's and D's caches, D reads one request from P, and the recorded descriptors
+# are run as memory copies so every byte can be checked. Each case is the
+# first layers of a model with that model's per-layer KV specs. Hybrid block
+# sizes are the ones vLLM aligns to on CPU, where the attention page must hold
+# the Mamba state.
+_BF16 = torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _attn(heads, head, head_v=None, window=None):
+    def make(block_size, _mamba_page):
+        kwargs = dict(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=heads,
+            head_size=head,
+            head_size_v=head_v or head,
+            dtype=_BF16,
+        )
+        if window is not None:
+            return SlidingWindowSpec(sliding_window=window, **kwargs)
+        return FullAttentionSpec(**kwargs)
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _mla(head=576, dtype=_BF16, **kwargs):
+    def make(block_size, _mamba_page):
+        return MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=head,
+            dtype=dtype,
+            **kwargs,
+        )
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _mamba(shapes, mamba_type):
+    def make(block_size, mamba_page):
+        return MambaSpec(
+            block_size=block_size,
+            shapes=shapes,
+            dtypes=(_BF16, torch.float32),
+            page_size_padded=mamba_page,
+            mamba_type=mamba_type,
+        )
+
+    return make
+
+
+def _layers(n, make):
+    return [entry for i in range(n) for entry in make(i)]
+
+
+_GDN = MambaAttentionBackendEnum.GDN_ATTN
+# (block size, [(layer name, spec factory)]) per model.
+_REAL_MODELS = {
+    # GLM-4.5-Air and MiniMax-M2 have the same attention shape.
+    "Qwen3-8B": (
+        128,
+        _layers(4, lambda i: [(f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _attn(8, 128))]),
+    ),
+    "gpt-oss-20b": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            4,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.attn.attn",
+                    _attn(8, 64, window=None if i % 2 else 128),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "gemma-3-1b": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            12,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _attn(1, 256, window=None if i % 6 == 5 else 512),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "MiMo-V2-Flash": (
+        128,
+        _layers(
+            12,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _attn(4, 192, 128)
+                    if i in (0, 5, 11)
+                    else _attn(8, 192, 128, window=128),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    # Kimi-K2 has the same MLA cache.
+    "DeepSeek-V3": (
+        128,
+        _layers(4, lambda i: [(f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _mla())]),
+    ),
+    "DeepSeek-V3.2": (
+        64,
+        _layers(
+            4,
+            lambda i: [
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn",
+                    _mla(is_index_group_leader=True),
+                ),
+                (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.indexer.k_cache",
+                    _mla(132, torch.uint8, cache_role=SparseCacheRole.INDEXER),
+                ),
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B": (
+        1152,
+        _layers(
+            8,
+            lambda i: [
+                (f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.attn", _attn(2, 256))
+                if i % 4 == 3
+                else (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.linear_attn",
+                    _mamba(((8192, 3), (32, 128, 128)), _GDN),
+                )
+            ],
+        ),
+    ),
+    "NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2": (
+        1408,
+        _layers(
+            22,
+            lambda i: (
+                [
+                    (
+                        f"model.layers.{i}.mixer",
+                        _mamba(
+                            ((12288, 3), (128, 80, 128)),
+                            MambaAttentionBackendEnum.MAMBA2,
+                        ),
+                    )
+                ]
+                if i in (0, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 20)
+                else [(f"model.layers.{i}.mixer.attn", _attn(8, 128))]
+                if i in (14, 21)
+                else []
+            ),
+        ),
+    ),
+    # KDA at 1-based layers 1-3, 5-7; MLA at 4 and 8. A 1920-token MLA page
+    # (64-token kernel blocks) is the first to hold the 2,170,880 B KDA state.
+    "Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B": (
+        1920,
+        _layers(

+            lambda i: [

+                if i % 4 == 3
+                else (
+                    f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn",
+                    _mamba(((12288, 3), (32, 128, 128)), _GDN),

+        ),
+    ),

+_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE = ["LBNHC", "LBHNC", "BLNHC", "BLHNC", "BHLNC", "LHBNC"]
+
+
+def _real_model_side(model, layout):
+    """Plan and allocate one side's KV caches the way the engine does, with
+    just enough blocks for one request of one or two blocks per group."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import resolve_kv_cache_layout
+    from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import (
+        get_global_kv_cache_groups,
+        get_kv_cache_configs,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.worker.utils import allocate_kv_cache
+
+    block_size, layers = _REAL_MODELS[model]
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size, max_model_len=block_size, kv_role="kv_both"
+    )
+    vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len = block_size
+    vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = layout
+    vllm_config.kv_transfer_config.kv_buffer_device = "cuda"
+    # A Mamba page is padded to the attention page, which holds it.
+    specs = {name: make(block_size, None) for name, make in layers}
+    mamba_page = max(
+        (
+            spec.page_size_bytes
+            for spec in specs.values()
+            if not isinstance(spec, MambaSpec)
+        ),
+        default=None,
+    )
+    specs = {name: make(block_size, mamba_page) for name, make in layers}
+    resolved = resolve_kv_cache_layout(
+        vllm_config, [_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE], specs.values()
+    )
+    groups = get_global_kv_cache_groups(vllm_config, [specs])
+    vllm_config.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks_override = 2 + sum(
+        _blocks_per_request(g.kv_cache_spec) for g in groups
+    )
+    kv_cache_config = get_kv_cache_configs(vllm_config, [specs], [1 << 40], groups)[0]
+    kv_cache_config.kv_cache_layout = vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout
+    caches = allocate_kv_cache(
+        kv_cache_config,
+        torch.device("cpu"),
+        resolved,
+        [g.kv_cache_spec.block_size for g in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups],
+    )
+    return vllm_config, kv_cache_config, caches
+
+
+def _blocks_per_request(spec):
+    return 1 if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec) else 2
+
+
+def _real_model_worker(engine_id, vllm_config, kv_cache_config, caches):
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.worker import (
+        NixlConnectorWorker,
+    )
+
+    use_mla = any(
+        isinstance(g.kv_cache_spec, MLAAttentionSpec)
+        for g in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups
+    )
+    fake_backend = MagicMock()
+    fake_backend.get_name.return_value = "FLASHMLA" if use_mla else "FLASH_ATTN"
+    fake_backend.full_cls_name.return_value = "fake.backend"
+    fake_platform = MagicMock()
+    fake_platform.device_type = "cuda"
+    fake_platform.get_nixl_memory_type.return_value = "VRAM"
+    with (
+        patch.object(bw, "NixlWrapper", _RecordingNixl),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_tensor_model_parallel_rank", return_value=0),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size", return_value=1),
+        patch.object(bw, "get_current_attn_backends", return_value=[fake_backend]),
+        patch.object(bw, "select_common_block_size", lambda size, *_: size),
+        patch.object(bw, "current_platform", fake_platform),
+        patch(
+            "vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils.get_conv_state_layout",
+            return_value="DS",
+        ),
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+    ):
+        worker = NixlConnectorWorker(vllm_config, engine_id, kv_cache_config)
+        worker.use_mla = use_mla

+    return worker
+
+
+def _cache_pages(cache, block):
+    """A layer's page(s) for one block: one tensor, or one per Mamba state."""
+    return (
+        [c[block] for c in cache]
+        if isinstance(cache, (list, tuple))
+        else [cache[block]]
+    )
+
+
+def _tag(page, *key):
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(hash(key) & 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    return torch.randint(1, 120, page.shape, generator=gen).to(page.dtype)
+
+
+def _run_recorded_copies(nixl):
+    """Run every recorded READ as memcpy: remote desc bytes -> local desc."""
+    import ctypes
+
+    for op, local_handle, local_ids, remote_handle, remote_ids in nixl.xfers:
+        assert op == "READ" and len(local_ids) == len(remote_ids)
+        for local_id, remote_id in zip(local_ids, remote_ids):
+            dst, dst_len, _ = (int(x) for x in nixl.dlists[local_handle][local_id])
+            src, src_len, _ = (int(x) for x in nixl.dlists[remote_handle][remote_id])
+            assert dst_len == src_len
+            ctypes.memmove(dst, src, dst_len)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test

+        ("DeepSeek-V3", "BLNHC", "LBNHC"),
+        ("Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B", "BLHNC", "BLHNC"),
+        ("NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2", "BLHNC", "BLHNC"),
+        ("Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B", "BLNHC", "BLNHC"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_real_model_layout_pull_copies_every_page(model, p_layout, d_layout):
+    """D pulls one request from P with each model's real KV plan: every page
+    of every layer arrives at D's block for the same layer and request
+    position, and nothing else in D's caches changes."""
+    from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.metadata import (
+        NixlConnectorMetadata,

+    p = _real_model_worker("P", p_config, p_kv_config, p_caches)
+    d = _real_model_worker("D", d_config, d_kv_config, d_caches)
+
+    # Block ids run up from 1 on P and down from the last block on D.
+    groups = d_kv_config.transfer_groups
+    p_ids: list[list[int]] = []
+    d_ids: list[list[int]] = []
+    for g in groups:
+        n = _blocks_per_request(g.kv_cache_spec)
+        p_ids.append([1 + sum(map(len, p_ids)) + k for k in range(n)])
+        d_ids.append(

+@pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invert_global_scales", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("experts_per_chunk", [1, 2, 3, 8])
+def test_dequantize_nvfp4_moe_weights_chunked_matches_full(
+    experts_per_chunk: int, invert_global_scales: bool, monkeypatch
+) -> None:
+    """Chunked dequantization must equal the single-chunk dequantization exactly.
+
+    5 experts cover one expert per chunk, a smaller last chunk (2, 3) and a
+    chunk larger than the number of experts (8).
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    device = torch.device(current_platform.device_type)
+    num_experts, hidden, inter, group = 5, 64, 32, 16
+
+    def packed(rows: int, cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.randint(
+            0, 256, (num_experts, rows, cols // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+        )
+
+    def block_scale(rows: int, cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        scale = torch.rand(num_experts, rows, cols // group, device=device) * 4 + 0.5
+        return scale.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+    w13_packed, w13_scale = packed(2 * inter, hidden), block_scale(2 * inter, hidden)
+    w2_packed, w2_scale = packed(hidden, inter), block_scale(hidden, inter)
+    w13_global = torch.rand(num_experts, 2, device=device) + 0.5
+    w2_global = torch.rand(num_experts, device=device) + 0.5
+
+    args = (w13_packed, w13_scale, w13_global, w2_packed, w2_scale, w2_global)
+    dtype = torch.float32
+    # The default chunk budget holds all experts at once.
+    ((_, expected_w13, expected_w2),) = (
+        nvfp4_emulation_utils.dequantize_nvfp4_moe_weights(
+            *args, dtype, invert_global_scales=invert_global_scales
+        )
+    )
+
+    expert_bytes = dtype.itemsize * 2 * (w13_packed[0].numel() + w2_packed[0].numel())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        nvfp4_emulation_utils,
+        "_DEQUANT_CHUNK_BYTES",
+        experts_per_chunk * expert_bytes,
+    )
+    chunks = list(
+        nvfp4_emulation_utils.dequantize_nvfp4_moe_weights(
+            *args, dtype, invert_global_scales=invert_global_scales
+        )
+    )
+
+    expected_starts = list(range(0, num_experts, experts_per_chunk))
+    assert [c[0].start for c in chunks] == expected_starts
+    assert chunks[-1][0].stop == num_experts
+    assert torch.equal(torch.cat([c[1] for c in chunks]), expected_w13)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.cat([c[2] for c in chunks]), expected_w2)

+def test_gfx942_moe_weight_quant_avoids_dynamic_per_token_op(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """gfx942 load-time MoE quantization uses the torch per-channel path."""
+    device = current_platform.device_type
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    w13_weight = torch.randn(2, 96, 128, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w2_weight = torch.randn(2, 128, 48, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    method = object.__new__(Fp8PtpcOnlineMoEMethod)
+    method.moe = SimpleNamespace(tp_size=1)
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(local_num_experts=2)
+
+    def fail_dynamic_quant(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise AssertionError("gfx942 must not call dynamic per-token FP8 quant")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "scaled_fp8_quant", fail_dynamic_quant)
+    with (
+        mock.patch.object(
+            method,
+            "get_weights_for_quantization",
+            return_value=(w13_weight, w2_weight),
+        ) as get_weights,
+        mock.patch.object(method, "_setup_kernel") as setup_kernel,
+        mock.patch.object(
+            method, "release_requantization_source_weights"
+        ) as release_weights,
+    ):
+        method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    get_weights.assert_called_once_with(layer)

+    release_weights.assert_called_once_with(layer)
+    _, got_w13, got_w2, got_w13_scale, got_w2_scale = setup_kernel.call_args.args
+    assert setup_kernel.call_args.kwargs == {
+        "w13_input_scale": None,
+        "w2_input_scale": None,
+    }
+
+    fp8_min, fp8_max = get_fp8_min_max()
+
+    def reference(weight: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        fp8_max_tensor = torch.tensor(
+            fp8_max, device=weight.device, dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        scale = weight.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True).float() / fp8_max_tensor
+        scale.clamp_min_(1.0 / (fp8_max * 512))
+        quantized = (
+            (weight / scale).clamp(fp8_min, fp8_max).to(current_platform.fp8_dtype())
+        )
+        return quantized, scale
+
+    expected_w13, expected_w13_scale = reference(w13_weight)
+    expected_w2, expected_w2_scale = reference(w2_weight)

+        for rows, reference in (

+            (slice(intermediate_size, 2 * intermediate_size), up),
+        ):

 - `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`: Timeout (in seconds) for automatically releasing the prefiller’s KV cache for a particular request. (Optional)
     - Default: 480
     - If a request is aborted and the decoder has not yet notified the prefiller, the prefill instance will release its KV-cache blocks after this timeout to avoid holding them indefinitely.
+    - When `kv_lease_duration` is set, the lease decides when those blocks are released instead. This timeout still bounds how long a pull waits for a prefill that has not finished.
 
 ## KV Transfer Config
 
@@ -80,6 +81,10 @@ cache), see [ECMooncakeConnector Usage Guide](mooncake_ec_connector_usage.md).
 - **num_workers**: Size of thread pool for one prefiller worker to transfer KV caches by mooncake. (default 10)
 - **mooncake_protocol**: Mooncake connector protocol. (default "rdma")
 - **device_name**: Comma-separated whitelist of RDMA devices (e.g. `"mlx5_0,mlx5_1"`) to restrict topology discovery to. Empty discovers every device. Useful on hosts exposing a mix of InfiniBand and RoCE ports, where both peers must settle on the same link layer.
+- **kv_lease_duration**: Seconds the prefiller holds a finished request's KV blocks before the decoder must renew them. (default unset)
+    - Unset keeps the fixed `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.
+    - When set, the decoder renews the lease every `kv_lease_duration / 6` seconds from the time the request arrives until its pull settles, and each renewal extends it to at least `kv_lease_duration * 2 / 3` seconds from then, as in [NixlConnector](../design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md). Blocks of a decoder that crashed are freed within about `kv_lease_duration` seconds, while requests queued on a busy decoder keep their blocks.
+    - Set the same value on prefill and decode instances. A decoder without it does not renew, so its requests that wait longer than the lease lose their prefilled KV; a prefiller without it rejects renewals, and the decoder logs a warning. Prefill instances from releases without this option log an error for each renewal they receive, so upgrade them before enabling it on decode instances.
 - **bootstrap_server_address**: Optional `"host:port"` of an already running Mooncake bootstrap server. All prefiller ranks register with this endpoint instead of launching an embedded server. The caller owns the server lifetime and must configure the proxy to use the same endpoint. The example proxy assumes the bootstrap server is on the prefiller API host; a different host requires a proxy that supplies that address in `remote_bootstrap_addr`. Omit this option to use the embedded server and `VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT`.

+"""Engram host tables in host-NUMA cuMem, shared across DP ranks by FABRIC handle.
+
+GPUs map cuMem host memory with 2M pages instead of the 64K pages of a registered
+/dev/shm mapping, so random row lookups miss the TLB far less.
+"""
+
+import ctypes
+import weakref
+from functools import cache
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cu
+
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import GroupCoordinator
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.engram import describe_error, gather_errors
+from vllm.utils.cpu_resource_utils import get_memory_node_info
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+FABRIC_HANDLE = cu.CUmemAllocationHandleType.CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC
+# Tables are created in chunks, so the creator can stop before draining its node.
+CHUNK_BYTES = 2 << 30
+# Fraction of the NUMA node left to other allocations.
+NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION = 0.05
+
+
+class ExportedHostTable(NamedTuple):
+    """What a peer needs to map a table."""
+
+    numa_node: int
+    padded_bytes: int
+    fabric_handles: list[bytes]
+
+
+def _chunk_ranges(padded_bytes: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    return [
+        (offset, min(CHUNK_BYTES, padded_bytes - offset))
+        for offset in range(0, padded_bytes, CHUNK_BYTES)
+    ]
+
+
+def _call_driver(fn, *args):
+    """Call a CUDA driver API and return its result, raising on failure."""
+    error, *result = fn(*args)
+    if error != cu.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{fn.__name__} failed: {error.name}")
+    return result[0] if result else None
+
+
+def _gpu_numa_node() -> int:
+    return _call_driver(
+        cu.cuDeviceGetAttribute,
+        cu.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID,
+        torch.accelerator.current_device_index(),
+    )
+
+
+def _host_allocation_prop(numa_node: int) -> cu.CUmemAllocationProp:
+    prop = cu.CUmemAllocationProp()
+    prop.type = cu.CUmemAllocationType.CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED
+    prop.location.type = cu.CUmemLocationType.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA
+    prop.location.id = numa_node
+    prop.requestedHandleTypes = FABRIC_HANDLE
+    return prop
+
+
+def _allocation_granularity(prop: cu.CUmemAllocationProp) -> int:
+    return _call_driver(cu.cuMemGetAllocationGranularity, prop, 0)
+
+
+def _export_fabric_handle(handle) -> bytes:
+    exported = _call_driver(cu.cuMemExportToShareableHandle, handle, FABRIC_HANDLE, 0)
+    return bytes(exported.data)
+
+
+def _release(handles: list) -> None:
+    for handle in handles:
+        cu.cuMemRelease(handle)
+
+
+def _read_write_access(location_type, location_id: int) -> cu.CUmemAccessDesc:
+    access = cu.CUmemAccessDesc()
+    access.location.type = location_type
+    access.location.id = location_id
+    access.flags = cu.CUmemAccess_flags.CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READWRITE
+    return access
+
+
+def _unmap(address: int, size: int, ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> None:
+    for offset, length in ranges:
+        cu.cuMemUnmap(address + offset, length)
+    cu.cuMemAddressFree(address, size)
+
+

+def fabric_host_memory_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether host-NUMA cuMem allocations can export FABRIC handles here."""
+    try:
+        prop = _host_allocation_prop(_gpu_numa_node())
+        handle = _call_driver(cu.cuMemCreate, _allocation_granularity(prop), prop, 0)
+        try:
+            _export_fabric_handle(handle)
+        finally:
+            cu.cuMemRelease(handle)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Host-NUMA cuMem FABRIC handles are unavailable (%s); Engram DP "
+            "replicas share tables through /dev/shm.",
+            exc,
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _create_table(num_bytes: int) -> tuple[list, ExportedHostTable]:
+    """Allocate and export a table on this GPU's host NUMA node.
+
+    Stops once the node would drop below its reserve. The kernel compacts to
+    find 2M pages and fails the chunk, rather than OOM-killing, if it cannot.
+    """
+    numa_node = _gpu_numa_node()

+    padded_bytes = round_up(num_bytes, _allocation_granularity(prop))
+    reserve = get_memory_node_info(numa_node).total_memory * NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION

+    try:
+        for offset, length in _chunk_ranges(padded_bytes):
+            handles.append(_call_driver(cu.cuMemCreate, length, prop, 0))
+            if get_memory_node_info(numa_node).available_memory < reserve:
+                raise MemoryError(
+                    f"NUMA node {numa_node} fell below its "
+                    f"{reserve / 2**30:.1f} GiB reserve after "
+                    f"{(offset + length) / 2**30:.1f} of "
+                    f"{padded_bytes / 2**30:.1f} GiB"
+                )
+        exported = [_export_fabric_handle(handle) for handle in handles]
+    except BaseException:
+        _release(handles)

+
+def _map_table(
+    table: ExportedHostTable, num_bytes: int, handles: list

+        location = cu.CUmemLocationType

+            _read_write_access(location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE, device),
+            _read_write_access(
+                location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA, table.numa_node
+            ),
+        ]
+        _call_driver(
+            cu.cuMemSetAccess, address, table.padded_bytes, access, len(access)
+        )
+    except BaseException:
+        if address is not None:
+            _unmap(address, table.padded_bytes, mapped)
+        raise

+        # The mappings keep the allocations alive.
+        _release(handles)

+    host_buffer = (ctypes.c_uint8 * num_bytes).from_address(address)
+    finalizer = weakref.finalize(
+        host_buffer, _unmap, address, table.padded_bytes, mapped

+    finalizer.atexit = False  # type: ignore[misc]

+    # Name the device: an index-less "cuda" makes torch copy the table.
+    gpu_view = torch.as_tensor(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            __cuda_array_interface__={
+                "shape": (num_bytes,),
+                "typestr": "|u1",
+                "data": (address, False),
+                "version": 3,
+            },
+            owner=host_buffer,
+        ),
+        device=torch.device("cuda", device),
+    )
+    return torch.frombuffer(host_buffer, dtype=torch.uint8), gpu_view

+
+def share_host_table(
+    num_bytes: int, group: GroupCoordinator
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
+    """Map one table on every rank of a node-local group, or None on all of them.

+# ------------------------------------------------------------------
+# FlyDSL JIT compilation hook
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------

+def _log_flydsl_jit_compile(fn_name: str, detail: str | None = None) -> None:
+    _handle_jit_event(
+        backend="FlyDSL",
+        event="JIT compilation",
+        fn_name=fn_name,
+        detail=detail,
+    )
+
+
+def _flydsl_kernel_symbols(module: object, infer_kernel_names) -> str | None:
+    """Name the ``gpu.func`` kernels in a module about to be compiled.
+
+    ``func_name`` is the Python launcher name, which many kernels share
+    verbatim (``launch``), so the ``gpu.func`` symbols are what identify the
+    kernel and the width that needs warmup.
+    """
+    if module is None:
+        return None
+    names = dict.fromkeys(infer_kernel_names(str(module)))
+    return "kernels=" + ",".join(names) if names else None

+

+    except ImportError:
+        logger.debug("FlyDSL is not available; skipping FlyDSL JIT monitor.")
+        return
+

+        # MlirCompiler.compile is called only on a cache miss, so for now
+        # we don't monitor disk cache hits
+        original_compile = compiler_cls.compile
+        # TODO: use a public API
+        infer_kernel_names = jit_function._infer_kernel_names_from_asm
+    except AttributeError as exc:

+            "FlyDSL JIT monitoring is disabled; its JIT internals moved (%s).", exc
+        )
+        return
+
+    @functools.wraps(original_compile)

+        detail = None

+            detail = _flydsl_kernel_symbols(module, infer_kernel_names)
+        _log_flydsl_jit_compile(str(kwargs.get("func_name") or "<unknown>"), detail)
+        return original_compile(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    compiler_cls.compile = classmethod(_compile_with_monitor)
+    _flydsl_hook_installed = True

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""EPLB replica mapping and expert-load recording shared by Triton kernels."""
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def eplb_map_and_record(
+    logical_ids,
+    token_idx,
+    mask,
+    logical_to_physical,
+    replica_count,
+    num_logical,
+    map_stride,
+    expert_load,
+    num_physical,
+    record_enabled,
+    num_unpadded_tokens,
+):
+    """Map logical expert ids to physical replicas and record expert load.
+
+    ``token_idx`` broadcasts against ``logical_ids``; masked-off or
+    out-of-range ids map to -1.
+    """
+    valid = mask & (logical_ids >= 0) & (logical_ids < num_logical)
+    safe_ids = tl.where(valid, logical_ids, 0)
+    replicas = tl.load(replica_count + safe_ids, mask=valid, other=1)
+    # floor(2^32 / phi), classic Knuth multiplicative hash multiplier.
+    KNUTH_MULTIPLIER = 2654435769
+    hashed = (token_idx.to(tl.int64) * KNUTH_MULTIPLIER) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    physical_ids = tl.load(
+        logical_to_physical + safe_ids * map_stride + hashed % replicas,
+        mask=valid,
+        other=-1,
+    )
+
+    record = (
+        (tl.load(record_enabled) != 0)
+        & (physical_ids >= 0)
+        & (physical_ids < num_physical)
+    )
+    if num_unpadded_tokens is not None:
+        record &= token_idx < tl.load(num_unpadded_tokens)
+    tl.atomic_add(expert_load + tl.where(record, physical_ids, 0), 1, mask=record)
+    return physical_ids

Signed-off-by: Glen Messenger <57537684+glenmessenger@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

new file mode 100644
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+# k8s-aibom
+
+[k8s-aibom](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-aibom) is an open-source Kubernetes controller that keeps an inventory of the AI workloads actually serving in a cluster. For every vLLM deployment it produces a [CycloneDX ML-BOM](https://cyclonedx.org/capabilities/mlbom/): the vLLM image and resolved digest, the model the server was started with, and, when the model is signed, the verified signer identity. Each attribute carries the evidence it was read from and a confidence tier (declared, inferred, or unresolved).
+
+It is read-only toward your cluster: it watches workloads through the Kubernetes API, adds no sidecars or init containers, runs unprivileged, and never changes scheduling or serving behavior. vLLM is detected whether you run it as a plain Deployment or StatefulSet, as a LeaderWorkerSet or DisaggregatedSet, under [KubeAI](kubeai.md), [KServe](kserve.md), [KubeRay](kuberay.md), [llm-d](llm-d.md), or the [production stack](production-stack.md), which ships it as an optional chart dependency.
+
+## Install
+
+```bash
+helm install k8s-aibom oci://ghcr.io/googlecloudplatform/charts/k8s-aibom \
+  --version 1.6.0 \
+  --namespace k8s-aibom-system --create-namespace
+```
+
+Then opt in each namespace that serves models:
+
+```bash
+kubectl label namespace <your-serving-namespace> aibom.k8saibom.dev/enabled=true
+```
+
+Documents appear as `AIBOM` resources next to the workloads they describe. The `kubectl aibom` plugin (`kubectl krew install aibom`) summarizes and searches them:
+
+```bash
+kubectl aibom summary -A
+kubectl aibom find --runtime vllm -A
+kubectl aibom find --image vllm/vllm-openai -A
+```
+
+See the [k8s-aibom documentation](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-aibom#readme) for the document format, signature verification, external sinks, and the full list of detected runtimes.

+    def load_weights(
+        self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]

+    def _detect_mixtral_format(

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""pytest plugin for AMD CI jobs: leave without native teardown once pytest is done.
+
+A pytest process can crash in native library destructors after its summary:
+vllm/ci #96786 printed "236 passed" and then died with SIGSEGV (exit 139) during
+interpreter shutdown, past the point where faulthandler reports. Once the outermost
+session has finished, this runs the Python exit handlers (engine shutdown, Ray,
+multiprocessing cleanup), flushes, and exits with pytest's own status, skipping
+module teardown and native destructors. pytest's result is never changed, and a
+command chain still stops on a real failure.
+
+Off when a kernel recorder is loaded (it writes its trace during native teardown)
+or with VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT=0.
+"""
+
+import atexit
+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+_outer = None
+_session = None
+
+
+def _recorder_loaded() -> bool:
+    return bool(
+        os.environ.get("ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES")
+        or os.environ.get("CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH")
+        or "rocprofiler" in os.environ.get("LD_PRELOAD", "")
+    )
+
+
+def pytest_configure(config):
+    global _outer
+    if _outer is None:  # pytester runs nested sessions in-process; act on the outer one
+        _outer = config
+
+
+def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
+    global _session
+    if session.config is _outer:
+        _session = session
+
+
+@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)
+def pytest_unconfigure(config):
+    if config is not _outer or _session is None:
+        return
+    if os.environ.get("VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT") == "0" or _recorder_loaded():
+        return
+    status = int(_session.exitstatus)
+    sys.stdout.flush()
+    sys.stderr.flush()
+    try:
+        atexit._run_exitfuncs()
+    except BaseException as exc:  # an exit handler failing must not mask the result
+        print(f"[amd-ci] exit handler failed: {exc!r}", file=sys.stderr)
+    print(
+        f"[amd-ci] pytest finished with exit {status}; leaving without native teardown",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    sys.stdout.flush()
+    os._exit(status)

-###############################################################################
-# Pytest marker/keyword re-quoting
-#
-# When commands are passed through Buildkite -> shell -> $* -> bash -c,
-# quotes around multi-word pytest -m/-k expressions get stripped:
-#   pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' v1/core
-# becomes:
-#   pytest -v -s -m not cpu_test v1/core
-#
-# pytest then interprets "cpu_test" as a file path, not part of the marker.
-#
-# This function detects unquoted expressions after -m/-k and re-quotes them
-# by collecting tokens until a recognizable boundary is reached:
-#   - test path (contains '/')
-#   - test file (ends with '.py')
-#   - another pytest flag (--xxx or -x single-char flags)
-#   - command separator (&& || ; |)
-#   - environment variable assignment (FOO=bar)
-#
-# Single-word markers (e.g. -m cpu_test, -m hybrid_model) pass through
-# unquoted since they have no spaces and work fine.
-#
-# Already-quoted expressions (containing literal single quotes) are passed
-# through untouched to avoid double-quoting well-formed shell fragments.
-#
-# NOTE: This ONLY fixes -m/-k flags. It cannot recover arbitrary inner
-# double-quotes stripped by the calling shell (see header comment).
-# Use VLLM_TEST_COMMANDS to avoid the problem entirely.
-###############################################################################
-re_quote_pytest_markers() {
-  local input="$1"
-  local output=""
-  local collecting=false
-  local marker_buf=""
-
-  # Strip backslash-newline continuations, then flatten remaining newlines
-  local flat="${input//$'\\\n'/ }"
-  flat="${flat//$'\n'/ }"
-
-  # Disable globbing to prevent *.py etc. from expanding during read -ra
-  local restore_glob
-  restore_glob="$(shopt -p -o noglob 2>/dev/null || true)"
-  set -o noglob
-  local -a words
-  read -ra words <<< "$flat"
-  eval "$restore_glob"
-
-  for word in "${words[@]}"; do
-    if $collecting; then
-      # If the token we're about to collect already contains a literal
-      # single quote, the expression was already quoted upstream.
-      # Flush and stop collecting.
-      if [[ "$word" == *"'"* ]]; then
-        if [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-          # Should not normally happen (partial buf + quote), flush raw
-          output+="${marker_buf} "
-          marker_buf=""
-        fi
-        output+="${word} "
-        collecting=false
-        continue
-      fi
-
-      local is_boundary=false
-      case "$word" in
-        # Line-continuation artifact
-        "\\")
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Command separators
-        "&&"|"||"|";"|"|")
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Long flags (--ignore, --shard-id, etc.)
-        --*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Short flags (-v, -s, -x, etc.) but NOT negative marker tokens
-        # like "not" which don't start with "-". Also skip -k/-m which
-        # would start a new marker (handled below).
-        -[a-zA-Z])
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Test path (contains /)
-        */*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Test file (ends with .py, possibly with ::method)
-        *.py|*.py::*)
-          is_boundary=true ;;
-        # Environment variable assignment preceding a command (FOO=bar)
-        *=*)
-          # Only treat as boundary if it looks like VAR=value, not
-          # pytest filter expressions like num_gpus=2 inside markers
-          if [[ "$word" =~ ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*= ]]; then
-            is_boundary=true
-          fi
-          ;;
-      esac
-
-      if $is_boundary; then
-        # Strip surrounding double quotes if present (from upstream
-        # single-to-double conversion); without this, wrapping below
-        # would produce '"expr"' with literal double-quote characters.
-        if [[ "$marker_buf" == '"'*'"' ]]; then
-          marker_buf="${marker_buf#\"}"
-          marker_buf="${marker_buf%\"}"
-        fi
-        # Flush the collected marker expression
-        if [[ "$marker_buf" == *" "* || "$marker_buf" == *"("* ]]; then
-          output+="'${marker_buf}' "
-        else
-          output+="${marker_buf} "
-        fi
-        collecting=false
-        marker_buf=""
-        # Check if this boundary word itself starts a new -m/-k
-        if [[ "$word" == "-m" || "$word" == "-k" ]]; then
-          output+="${word} "
-          collecting=true
-        # Drop stray backslash tokens silently
-        elif [[ "$word" == "\\" ]]; then
-          :
-        else
-          output+="${word} "
-        fi
-      else
-        # Accumulate into marker buffer
-        if [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-          marker_buf+=" ${word}"
-        else
-          marker_buf="${word}"
-        fi
-      fi
-    elif [[ "$word" == "-m" || "$word" == "-k" ]]; then
-      output+="${word} "
-      collecting=true
-      marker_buf=""
-    else
-      output+="${word} "
-    fi
-  done
-
-  # Flush any trailing marker expression (marker at end of command)
-  if $collecting && [[ -n "$marker_buf" ]]; then
-    # Strip surrounding double quotes (see mid-stream flush comment)
-    if [[ "$marker_buf" == '"'*'"' ]]; then
-      marker_buf="${marker_buf#\"}"
-      marker_buf="${marker_buf%\"}"
-    fi
-    if [[ "$marker_buf" == *" "* || "$marker_buf" == *"("* ]]; then
-      output+="'${marker_buf}'"
-    else
-      output+="${marker_buf}"
-    fi
-  fi
-
-  echo "${output% }"
-}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Build and promote ROCm images via docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl.
+# Pushes only to $ROCM_CI_REPO and the BuildKit cache that goes with it.
+#
+# Usage: build.sh <stack> <mode>
+#
+# Modes:
+#   keys     Print current Ks/Kr keys and whether their images exist (on-call debug).
+#   base     Ensure stack, runtime and test-deps images exist; write their refs to Buildkite metadata.
+#   ci       Build and push this build's per-commit test image.
+#   release  Release image + wheels from source into the release repo (release pipeline, AWS agents).
+#   release-base  Only the release stack and runtime (a serialized step, so one run builds a new key).
+#
+# Stack: rocm (TheRock ROCm 10). Force a stack rebuild: bump ARG REFRESH
+#        in docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base
+#
+# Trust: ROCM_CI_REPO is set by ci-infra (CI) or release-pipeline.yaml (release).
+#   Trusted main builds: rocm/vllm-ci
+#   PR / fork builds:    rocm/vllm-dev    (pr<N>- tags and caches; trusted builds never read it)
+#   Other untrusted:     rocm/vllm-dev    (br-<branch>-<hash>- tags and caches: nightlies, branch builds)
+#   Release pipeline:    its ECR repo     (never reads rocm/vllm-ci or its cache: it builds the
+#                                          stack and runtime from source, with only its own ECR cache;
+#                                          csrc objects come from the shared S3 sccache, as in CUDA)
+# ROCM_CI_TRUSTED_REPO / ROCM_CI_CACHE_REPO only point a local run at a sandbox registry.
+set -euo pipefail
+

+# Arguments and trust
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+STACK=$1
+MODE=$2
+REPO=${ROCM_CI_REPO:?ROCM_CI_REPO must be set (by ci-infra or release-pipeline.yaml)}
+TRUSTED=${ROCM_CI_TRUSTED_REPO:-rocm/vllm-ci}

+  fi
+  CACHE_TO=$REPO:cache-$PFX
+  # Only the compile stages' cache: everything else is cheap or in the trusted cache.
+  export CACHE_CI=false
+fi

+case $STACK in
+  rocm) SDF=docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base ;;
+  *) echo "Unknown stack: $STACK" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# BuildKit builder
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Prefer the host buildkitd (it has its own GC policy and cache). Fall back
+# to a docker-container builder if no socket is present. Release RUN steps must reach EC2 IMDS
+# for sccache's S3 credentials: their fallback builder uses the host network, under its own name.
+B=vllm-rocm net=()
+[[ $MODE == release* ]] && B=vllm-rocm-release net=(--driver-opt network=host)

+  if [[ -S /run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock ]]; then
+    drv=(--driver remote unix:///run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock)
+  else
+    drv=(--driver docker-container "${net[@]}" \
+      ${BUILDKITD_CONFIG:+--buildkitd-config "$BUILDKITD_CONFIG"})
+  fi
+  # || inspect: tolerate a race where another job created it between the check and create.
+  docker buildx create --name "$B" "${drv[@]}" >/dev/null \
+    || docker buildx inspect "$B" >/dev/null
+fi

+docker buildx version
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Build context — an export of HEAD
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Bake builds .rocm-src, not the checkout: the content keys below hash HEAD, and BuildKit keys
+# COPY on file modes, which drift on shared agents. umask 022 gives every agent git's modes.
+[[ $(git rev-parse HEAD) == $(git rev-parse "${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:-HEAD}^{commit}") ]] \
+  || { echo "HEAD is not BUILDKITE_COMMIT ($BUILDKITE_COMMIT)" >&2; exit 1; }

+rm -rf .rocm-src && mkdir .rocm-src
+git archive HEAD | tar -x --no-same-permissions -C .rocm-src -f -
+export CONTEXT=.rocm-src

+# Git tags — required by the version stage
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# setuptools_scm needs a reachable v* tag. Agents clone without tags, partially
+# and with their objects in a host mirror (--reference) that the build context
+# cannot see; --force updates tags that moved (e.g. a re-tag after a release

+  "$(git log -1 --format=%cI)" "$(git describe --tags --long --abbrev=40 --match 'v[0-9]*')" \
+  > .rocm-src/.git_archival.txt
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helper functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# digest <ref>
+#   Print the sha256 digest of <ref>. Returns 1 if the tag does not exist.
+#   The "Digest:" line of the plain output is parsed and validated (as the old CI
+#   scripts did): --format output and stray stderr are not safe to splice into a ref.
+#   Any other registry error, after retries, exits 75 (the steps retry it); in a $()
+#   subshell that becomes the substitution's status, which ensure() and set -e pass on.
+digest() {
+  local out rc d try
+  for try in 1 2 3; do
+    rc=0
+    out=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" 2>&1) || rc=$?
+    d=$(awk '$1 == "Digest:" { print $2; exit }' <<<"$out")

+    if ((rc != 0)) && grep -qiE 'manifest unknown|no such manifest|name unknown|not found|does not exist' <<<"$out"; then
+      return 1
+    fi
+    ((try == 3)) || sleep 5
+  done
+  echo "registry error for $1 (exit $rc): $out" >&2
+  exit 75
+}
+
+# label <ref> <key>  — read one image label
+label() { docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" \
+            --format "{{index .Image.Config.Labels \"$2\"}}"; }
+
+# bake <targets...>  — invoke docker buildx bake with the project HCL
+bake()   { docker buildx bake -f docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl "$@"; }
+
+# meta <get|set> <key> [value]  — Buildkite build metadata
+meta()   { buildkite-agent meta-data "$@"; }
+
+# pushed <bake-metadata-file> <target>  — the digest that bake pushed for <target>
+pushed() {
+  local d
+  d=$(awk -F'"' -v t="$2" '/^  "/ { k = $2 } k == t && $2 == "containerimage.digest" { print $4 }' "$1")
+  [[ $d =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] && echo "$d"
+}

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Content keys
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Ks (stack key): hash of the stack Dockerfile + therock_wheels.py.
+#   A Ks cache miss triggers a full stack rebuild (hours).
+# Kr (runtime key): Ks + the portion of Dockerfile.rocm above the per-commit
+#   marker + all pip requirement files.
+#   A Kr cache miss triggers a runtime rebuild (minutes).
+
+_trw=$( [[ $STACK == rocm ]] && echo tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py || true )

+# identity: an image left in an older format would hand later builds a second copy of the same layers.
+Ks=$( { echo "layers: zstd-3, mtimes kept"; git ls-tree HEAD -- "$SDF" ${_trw:+"$_trw"}; } | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
+Kr=$(
+  {
+    echo "$Ks"
+    sed '/^# ==== per-commit stages/q' .rocm-src/docker/Dockerfile.rocm
+    git ls-tree HEAD -- \
+      requirements/common.txt \
+      requirements/rocm.txt \
+      requirements/test/rocm.txt \
+      rust-toolchain.toml \
+      tests/vllm_test_utils \
+      tools/install_torchcodec_rocm.sh
+  } | sha256sum | cut -c1-16
+)
+echo "build.sh $STACK $MODE: repo=$REPO trusted=$TRUSTED Ks=$Ks Kr=$Kr"

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# ensure <bake-target> <tag-suffix> [<sibling-suffix>]
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Resolve a content-keyed image without building if it already exists.
+# Resolution order:
+#   1. Trusted registry (rocm/vllm-ci:<tag>) — safe for any CI build to reuse. Not for release:
+#      CI agents also run PR code, so release never ships an image it did not build itself.
+#   2. This repo's own tag ($REPO:$PFX<tag>) — PR builds and the release pipeline write here.
+#   3. Neither found: build via bake and push.
+# A <sibling-suffix> means the image only counts as present when the sibling
+# tag also exists (used by stack: must have both the image and -wheels); then
+# both pinned refs are printed, space-separated.
+ensure() {
+  local target=$1 tag=$2 sibling=${3:-} ref d ds refs rc mf
+  refs=("$REPO:$PFX$tag")
+  [[ $MODE == release* || $REPO == "$TRUSTED" ]] || refs=("$TRUSTED:$tag" "${refs[@]}")
+
+  for ref in "${refs[@]}"; do
+    if d=$(digest "$ref") && { [[ -z $sibling ]] || ds=$(digest "$ref$sibling"); }; then
+      echo "Reusing $ref@$d" >&2
+      echo "$ref@$d${sibling:+ $ref$sibling@$ds}"
+      return 0
+    else
+      rc=$?; ((rc == 1)) || return $rc   # a registry error is not a miss
+    fi
+  done
+
+  # Neither copy found — build and push.
+  ref=$REPO:$PFX$tag
+  echo "--- :docker: Building $target as $ref" >&2
+  # Explicit checks: $(ensure ...) runs in a subshell, where set -e does not apply.
+  mf=$(mktemp)
+  TAG=$ref bake --metadata-file "$mf" "$target" >&2 || { rm -f "$mf"; echo "building $ref failed" >&2; return 1; }
+  # The digests this bake pushed (base: stack-<stack>, stack-wheels), not the tags', which by now
+  # may hold a concurrent build's push of the same key.
+  if ! d=$(pushed "$mf" "${target/#base/stack-$STACK}") \
+      || { [[ -n $sibling ]] && ! ds=$(pushed "$mf" stack-wheels); }; then
+    rm -f "$mf"; echo "bake recorded no digest for $ref" >&2; return 1
+  fi
+  rm -f "$mf"
+  echo "$ref@$d${sibling:+ $ref$sibling@$ds}"
+}
+
+# load — read stack/runtime refs from Buildkite metadata (written by base mode).
+load() {
+  STACK_IMAGE=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-stack")
+  STACK_WHEELS=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-stack-wheels")
+  RUNTIME=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-runtime")
+  TEST_DEPS=$(meta get "rocm-$STACK-test-deps")
+  export STACK_IMAGE STACK_WHEELS RUNTIME TEST_DEPS
+  for ref in "$STACK_IMAGE" "$STACK_WHEELS" "$RUNTIME" "$TEST_DEPS"; do
+    [[ $ref =~ @sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { echo "not a pinned image ref in the metadata: '$ref'" >&2; exit 1; }
+  done
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mode dispatch
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+case $MODE in
+
+  keys)
+    # Print current content keys and registry status (useful for on-call triage).
+    for t in "stack-$STACK-$Ks" "runtime-$STACK-$Kr" "test-deps-$STACK-$Kr"; do

+    done
+    ;;

+  base)

+    # so the ci mode can pull them without re-resolving.
+    # The "base" bake group builds the stack and its -wheels sibling together.
+    STACK_IMAGE=$(ensure base "stack-$STACK-$Ks" -wheels)
+    STACK_WHEELS=${STACK_IMAGE#* } STACK_IMAGE=${STACK_IMAGE%% *}
+    export STACK_IMAGE
+    RUNTIME=$(ensure runtime "runtime-$STACK-$Kr")
+    export RUNTIME
+    TEST_DEPS=$(ensure test-deps "test-deps-$STACK-$Kr")
+
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-stack"        "$STACK_IMAGE"
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-runtime"      "$RUNTIME"
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-test-deps"    "$TEST_DEPS"
+    meta set "rocm-$STACK-stack-wheels" "$STACK_WHEELS"
+    echo "stack=$STACK_IMAGE runtime=$RUNTIME test-deps=$TEST_DEPS stack-wheels=$STACK_WHEELS"
+    ;;
+
+  ci)
+    # Build and push the per-commit test image for GPU test steps.
+    load
+    export TAG=$REPO:build-$BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID
+    # AITER nightly (AITER_NIGHTLY=1 from the schedule): the test stage installs the newest
+    # AITER nightly that fits the image; an AITER_SPEC in the environment pins one instead.
+    rm -rf .rocm-wheel .rocm-kernel-map
+    bake ci
+    # For the python-only install test (run-amd-test.sh downloads it); not in the image.
+    buildkite-agent artifact upload ".rocm-wheel/vllm-*.whl"
+    # CI test selection (VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP=1, set by ci-infra): the kernel symbol map of this
+    # build's csrc, from the build cache. Optional: a missing map never fails the image build.
+    if [[ ${VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP:-0} == 1 ]]; then

+    fi
+    ;;
+
+  release|release-base)
+    # Build and push the release image + wheels into $REPO. The stack and runtime come from this
+    # repo only (built here once per key, from the same Dockerfiles and keys CI tests), never from
+    # rocm/vllm-ci or its cache.
+    STACK_IMAGE=$(ensure base "stack-$STACK-$Ks" -wheels)

+    [[ $MODE == release ]] || exit 0
+    export STACK_WHEELS RUNTIME
+    export TAG=$REPO:$STACK-$BUILDKITE_COMMIT
+

+    PUSH=false bake version
+    VLLM_VERSION=$(cat .rocm-version/vllm-version.txt)
+    export VLLM_VERSION

+        && [[ $(label "$TAG" org.opencontainers.image.version) == "$VLLM_VERSION" ]]; then
+      echo "Release image $TAG already exists with version $VLLM_VERSION — skipping." >&2
+      exit 0
+    fi
+
+    # Wheels first: their all-arch csrc compile is the long part, and vllm-openai reuses it.
+    bake wheels openai-smoke
+    # Alias the runtime as the -base tag (the base-nightly consumer reference).
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$TAG-base" "$RUNTIME"
+    # Push the vllm-openai tag last — its presence marks the set as complete.
+    bake vllm-openai
+    ;;
+
+  *)
+    echo "Unknown mode: $MODE" >&2
+    exit 2
+    ;;
+esac

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Promote ROCm release artifacts without rebuilding anything.
+# The release pipeline's build step (build.sh release) pushed the source images to
+# ECR; this script only copies digests and uploads wheels.
+#
+# Usage: publish.sh <stack> <mode>
+#
+# Modes:
+#   wheels   Extract the vLLM wheel from the -wheels image and upload to S3.
+#   images   Tag the release image and its runtime base for their variant in ECR.
+#            With NIGHTLY=1, also push the nightly tags to Docker Hub.
+#
+# Required environment variables:
+#   BUILDKITE_COMMIT   — the commit being released
+#   ECR            — ECR repository prefix (release-pipeline.yaml's ROCM_CI_REPO)
+#
+# Optional:
+#   HUB            — Docker Hub repo for nightly images (default: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm)
+#   NIGHTLY        — set to 1 to push nightly Hub tags (default: 0)
+#   DOCKERHUB_USERNAME — Hub username for cleanup script (default: vllmbot)
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Arguments
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+STACK=$1
+MODE=$2
+COMMIT=${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:?BUILDKITE_COMMIT must be set}
+
+ECR=${ECR:?ECR must be set (by release-pipeline.yaml)}
+SRC=$ECR:${STACK}-${COMMIT}   # build.sh release, in the same build
+HUB=${HUB:-vllm/vllm-openai-rocm}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helper functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# retry <cmd...>  — registry lookups: these steps have no retry rules
+retry() { "$@" || { sleep 5; "$@"; } || { sleep 5; "$@"; }; }
+
+# pin <ref>  — resolve <ref> to a pinned ref@digest (resolves once, stable for the rest of the script).
+#   Parses the validated "Digest:" line, as build.sh does.
+pin() {
+  local d
+  d=$(retry docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" | awk '$1 == "Digest:" { print $2; exit }')
+  [[ $d =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { echo "cannot resolve the digest of $1" >&2; return 1; }
+  echo "$1@$d"
+}
+
+# variant <ref>  — read the ai.vllm.rocm.variant image label
+variant() {
+  retry docker buildx imagetools inspect "$1" \
+    --format '{{index .Image.Config.Labels "ai.vllm.rocm.variant"}}'
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Resolve source image refs (done once; images step uses them too)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Logged in, the ECR lookups below are not subject to the anonymous rate limits.
+aws ecr-public get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
+  | docker login -u AWS --password-stdin "${ECR%%/*}"

+[[ $V =~ ^rocm[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "$IMG has no valid ai.vllm.rocm.variant label: '$V'" >&2; exit 1; }

+buildkite-agent meta-data set "rocm-$STACK-variant" "$V"
+

+# Mode dispatch
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  wheels)
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Extract the vLLM wheel from this commit's -wheels image and upload it
+  # to S3 so users can pip-install it directly.
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    WHEELS_IMG=$(pin "$SRC-wheels")
+
+    # Export wheel files out of the scratch image into ./dist/
+    rm -rf dist
+    echo "FROM $WHEELS_IMG" | docker buildx build -q -o dist -
+
+    # Sanity: the wheel's variant suffix must match the stack label.
+    # (setup.py's rocm_version_to_variant produces e.g. rocm100 for 10.0.x)
+    actual_variant=$(basename dist/vllm-*.whl | grep -oE 'rocm[0-9]+' | tail -1)

+      || { echo "Wheel variant $actual_variant != image variant $V" >&2; exit 1; }

+    bash .buildkite/scripts/upload-rocm-wheels.sh "$STACK" dist
+

+    WHL_URL="https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/$COMMIT/$V"
+    buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-wheels" << EOF
+## :package: ROCm \`$V\` wheels published
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant** | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**  | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **Branch**  | \`${BUILDKITE_BRANCH:-?}\` |
+
+### Install (this commit)
+\`\`\`bash
+pip install vllm --extra-index-url $WHL_URL
+\`\`\`
+
+### Install (latest nightly)
+\`\`\`bash
+pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly/$V
+\`\`\`
+
+### Download wheels directly
+\`\`\`bash
+aws s3 ls  s3://${S3_BUCKET:-vllm-wheels}/rocm/$COMMIT/$V-wheels/
+aws s3 cp  --recursive --exclude "*" --include "*.whl" s3://${S3_BUCKET:-vllm-wheels}/rocm/$COMMIT/$V-wheels/ .
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+    ;;
+
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  images)
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Tag the release image and its runtime base for their variant in ECR.
+  # With NIGHTLY=1, also tag them on Docker Hub and prune old nightly tags.
+  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    RT=$(pin "$SRC-base")    # runtime base alias (published as base-nightly*)
+
+    # --- ECR -----------------------------------------------------------------
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$ECR:$COMMIT-$V"       "$IMG"
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$ECR:$COMMIT-$V-base"  "$RT"
+
+    ECR_IMG="$ECR:$COMMIT-$V"
+    ECR_BASE="$ECR:$COMMIT-$V-base"
+
+    # --- Non-nightly annotation ----------------------------------------------
+    if [[ ${NIGHTLY:-0} != 1 ]]; then
+      buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-images" << EOF
+## :docker: ROCm \`$V\` images published to ECR
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant** | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**  | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **ECR image** | \`$ECR_IMG\` |
+| **ECR base**  | \`$ECR_BASE\` |
+
+\`\`\`bash
+docker pull $ECR_IMG
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+      exit 0
+    fi
+
+    # --- Nightly: Docker Hub -------------------------------------------------
+    export DOCKERHUB_USERNAME=${DOCKERHUB_USERNAME:-vllmbot}
+
+    # The default stack (rocm) owns the unqualified :nightly / :base-nightly tags.
+    # All stacks own the variant-qualified :nightly-<variant> tags.
+    suffixes=("-$V")
+    [[ $STACK == rocm ]] && suffixes+=("")
+
+    hub_tags=""
+    for sfx in "${suffixes[@]}"; do
+      docker buildx imagetools create \
+        -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$IMG"
+      docker buildx imagetools create \
+        -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$RT"
+      hub_tags="$hub_tags \`$HUB:nightly$sfx\` \`$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT\`"
+    done
+
+    # Prune old nightly tags (keep last 14 builds per tag family).
+    clean=.buildkite/scripts/cleanup-nightly-builds.sh
+    bash "$clean" "nightly-$V-"      "$HUB"
+    bash "$clean" "base-nightly-$V-" "$HUB"
+    if [[ $STACK == rocm ]]; then
+      bash "$clean" "nightly-"      "$HUB" "nightly-rocm"
+      bash "$clean" "base-nightly-" "$HUB" "base-nightly-rocm"
+    fi
+
+    buildkite-agent annotate --style success --context "rocm-$STACK-images" << EOF
+## :docker: ROCm \`$V\` nightly images published
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| **Variant**   | \`$V\` |
+| **Commit**    | \`$COMMIT\` |
+| **ECR image** | \`$ECR_IMG\` |
+| **ECR base**  | \`$ECR_BASE\` |
+| **Docker Hub** |$hub_tags |
+
+\`\`\`bash
+docker pull $HUB:nightly-$V
+\`\`\`
+EOF
+    ;;
+
+  *)
+    echo "Unknown mode: $MODE" >&2
+    exit 2
+    ;;
+esac

-resolve_image_digest() {
-    local image_ref="$1"
-    local attempts="${ROCM_IMAGE_DIGEST_ATTEMPTS:-4}"
-    local delay_secs="${ROCM_IMAGE_DIGEST_RETRY_DELAY:-2}"
-    local attempt=0
-    local output=""
-    local digest=""
-    local status=0
-
-    if [[ "${image_ref}" =~ @(sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})$ ]]; then
-        printf '%s\n' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
-        return 0
-    fi
-    if [[ ! "${attempts}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ \
-        || ! "${delay_secs}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
-        echo "Invalid image digest retry configuration" >&2
-        return 1
-    fi
-
-    for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt++)); do
-        status=0
-        output=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${image_ref}" 2>&1) || status=$?
-        digest=$(awk '$1 == "Digest:" { print $2; exit }' <<< "${output}")
-        if ((status == 0)) && [[ "${digest}" =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
-            printf '%s\n' "${digest}"
-            return 0
-        fi
-        if ((attempt < attempts)); then
-            printf \
-                'Image digest lookup failed for %s (%d/%d, status %d); retrying\n' \
-                "${image_ref}" "${attempt}" "${attempts}" "${status}" >&2
-            sleep "${delay_secs}"
-        fi
-    done
-
-    printf 'Failed to resolve digest for %s (status %d)\n%s\n' \
-        "${image_ref}" "${status}" "${output:-<no output>}" >&2
-    return 1
-}

-find_matching_base_content_ref() {

-    local remote_version=""
-    local attempts="${ROCM_IMAGE_DIGEST_ATTEMPTS:-4}"
-    local delay_secs="${ROCM_IMAGE_DIGEST_RETRY_DELAY:-2}"
-    local attempt=0
-    local inspect_status=0
-    shift 2
-
-    if [[ ! "${attempts}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ \
-        || ! "${delay_secs}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
-        echo "Invalid image identity retry configuration" >&2
-        return 1
-    fi
-
-    for image_ref in "$@"; do
-        if ! digest=$(resolve_image_digest "${image_ref}"); then
-            continue
-        fi
-        immutable_ref="${image_ref}@${digest}"
-        label_values=""
-        for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt++)); do
-            inspect_status=0
-            label_values=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${immutable_ref}" \
-                --format '{{ index .Image.Config.Labels "vllm.rocm_base.content_hash" }} {{ index .Image.Config.Labels "vllm.rocm_base.metadata_version" }}' \
-                2>/dev/null) || inspect_status=$?

-            remote_version=""

-                read -r remote_hash remote_version _ <<< "${label_values}"
-                if [[ "${remote_hash}" == "${expected_hash}" \
-                    && "${remote_version}" == "${expected_version}" ]]; then
-                    printf '%s\n' "${immutable_ref}"
-                    return 0
-                fi
-            fi
-            if ((attempt < attempts)); then
-                printf \
-                    'ROCm base identity lookup incomplete or mismatched for %s (%d/%d); retrying\n' \
-                    "${immutable_ref}" "${attempt}" "${attempts}" >&2
-                sleep "${delay_secs}"
-            fi
-        done
-        if ((inspect_status == 0)) \

-            echo "ROCm base content ref has unexpected identity: ${immutable_ref}" >&2

+"""The AMD CI pytest plugin skips native teardown without changing pytest's result."""
+
+import os
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+PLUGIN_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci"
+
+# An object that segfaults when the interpreter tears its module down, after the
+# summary, as native library destructors did in vllm/ci #96786.
+CRASH_AT_TEARDOWN = """
+import faulthandler
+
+class _CrashOnTeardown:
+    def __del__(self, _crash=faulthandler._sigsegv):
+        _crash()
+
+_keep = _CrashOnTeardown()
+"""
+
+
+def _run(tmp_path, body, *, plugin=True, env=None, args=()):
+    (tmp_path / "test_case.py").write_text(CRASH_AT_TEARDOWN + body)
+    run_env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "PYTEST_ADDOPTS"}
+    for name in ("ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES", "CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH", "VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT"):
+        run_env.pop(name, None)
+    run_env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(PLUGIN_DIR)
+    run_env.update(env or {})
+    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *args]
+    if plugin:
+        cmd += ["-p", "amd_ci_fast_exit"]
+    return subprocess.run(
+        [*cmd, "test_case.py"],
+        cwd=tmp_path,
+        env=run_env,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+
+
+PASSING = "\ndef test_ok():\n    assert True\n"
+
+
+def test_reproduces_the_teardown_crash_without_the_plugin(tmp_path):
+    assert _run(tmp_path, PASSING, plugin=False).returncode == -signal.SIGSEGV
+
+
+def test_a_passing_run_exits_zero_despite_the_teardown_crash(tmp_path):
+    result = _run(tmp_path, PASSING)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    assert "leaving without native teardown" in result.stderr
+
+
+def test_a_failing_run_keeps_its_exit_status(tmp_path):
+    result = _run(tmp_path, "\ndef test_bad():\n    assert False\n")
+    assert result.returncode == pytest.ExitCode.TESTS_FAILED
+
+
+def test_python_exit_handlers_still_run(tmp_path):
+    marker = tmp_path / "atexit-ran"
+    body = (
+        "\nimport atexit, pathlib\n"
+        f"atexit.register(pathlib.Path({str(marker)!r}).touch)\n" + PASSING
+    )
+    assert _run(tmp_path, body).returncode == 0
+    assert marker.exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "env",
+    [
+        {"VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT": "0"},
+        {"ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES": "/tmp/libkernrec_rocm.so"},
+        {"CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH": "/tmp/libkernrec.so"},
+    ],
+)
+def test_off_when_disabled_or_a_kernel_recorder_needs_native_teardown(tmp_path, env):
+    assert _run(tmp_path, PASSING, env=env).returncode == -signal.SIGSEGV
+
+
+def test_a_nested_in_process_session_does_not_end_the_outer_one(tmp_path):
+    body = (
+        "\npytest_plugins = ['pytester']\n"
+        "def test_inner_session(pytester):\n"
+        "    pytester.makepyfile('def test_x():\\n    assert True\\n')\n"
+        "    assert pytester.runpytest_inprocess('-p', 'amd_ci_fast_exit').ret == 0\n"
+        "\ndef test_after_the_inner_session():\n"
+        "    assert True\n"
+    )
+    result = _run(tmp_path, body)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
+    assert "2 passed" in result.stdout

+"""The ROCm image keys in .buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh must cover every
+build-context file the keyed Dockerfile parts read, or editing that file would
+ship a stale image."""
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path

+import pytest
+import regex as re

+ROOT = Path(__file__).parents[2]
+MARKER = "# ==== per-commit stages: nothing below is part of the runtime key ===="
+
+
+def context_sources(dockerfile: str) -> set[str]:
+    text = dockerfile.replace("\\\n", " ")
+    srcs = set()
+    for args in re.findall(r"^\s*(?:COPY|ADD)\s+(.*)$", text, re.M):
+        words = [w for w in args.split() if not w.startswith("--")]
+        if "--from=" not in args and not words[0].startswith("http"):
+            srcs.update(words[:-1])
+    for opts in re.findall(r"--mount=type=bind,(\S*)", text):
+        kv = dict(o.partition("=")[::2] for o in opts.split(","))
+        if "from" not in kv:
+            srcs.add(kv.get("source", kv.get("src", ".")))
+    return srcs
+
+
+def key_paths(name: str, stack: str = "") -> set[str]:
+    script = (ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh").read_text()
+    block_match = re.search(rf"^{name}=\$\(.*?sha256sum", script, re.M | re.S)
+    assert block_match is not None, f"{name}= block not found in build.sh"
+    pattern = r"\b(?:requirements|tools|tests)/[\w./-]+|\brust-toolchain\.toml\b"
+    paths = set(re.findall(pattern, block_match.group(0)))
+    # therock_wheels.py is injected into Ks via a helper variable (rocm stack only)
+    if name == "Ks" and stack == "rocm":
+        m = re.search(r"_[Tt][Rr][Ww]=.*?tools/[\w./-]+", script, re.S)
+        if m:
+            paths.update(re.findall(r"\b(?:requirements|tools)/[\w./-]+", m.group(0)))
+    return paths
+
+
+def test_runtime_key_covers_runtime_inputs():
+    dockerfile = (ROOT / "docker/Dockerfile.rocm").read_text()
+    assert dockerfile.count(MARKER) == 1
+    assert context_sources(dockerfile.split(MARKER)[0]) <= key_paths("Kr")
+
+
+def test_stack_key_covers_stack_inputs():
+    dockerfile = (ROOT / "docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base").read_text()
+    assert context_sources(dockerfile) <= key_paths("Ks", stack="rocm")

+def run_build(
